rationale: Owner answered all three open questions: docs-only project (no CLI implementation ticket), tool name/commands/copyright are fixed (jot; add/list/search/delete; Copyright 2026 Yazan), and STORAGE.md should target Python 3 in a single-user, single-machine, no-network, no-concurrent-writer context. With every prior unknown resolved, all four tickets can now be proposed consistently from the same shared facts. README/LICENSE/CHANGELOG are fully specified mechanical writing tasks assigned to the cheapest capable model (haiku); STORAGE.md is the one task requiring real trade-off analysis and is assigned to opus.

commands.title: Write README.md for jot
commands.description: Write README.md describing 'jot', a small note-taking CLI written in Python 3. Include a one-paragraph description of what the tool does and its core commands: `add` (create a note), `list` (show notes), `search` (full-text search notes), and `delete` (remove a note). Keep it concise -- a short usage example for each command is welcome but this is not a full user manual. Do not invent features beyond add/list/search/delete (e.g. no tags, no edit command, no sync) since those are not part of the tool's actual scope.
acceptance_criteria: README.md exists at the workspace root
Contains a one-paragraph description identifying the tool by name ('jot') and what it does
Documents exactly the four commands: add, list, search, delete -- no invented commands or features
Written in clear prose/Markdown, no placeholder or TODO text
commands.model_reason: Mechanical writing task with a fully fixed spec (tool name, commands, and format all given) -- no design judgment required.

commands.title: Write LICENSE.md with MIT text
commands.description: Write LICENSE.md containing the standard MIT License text, with copyright holder 'Yazan' and year 2026.
acceptance_criteria: LICENSE.md exists at the workspace root
Contains the full, unmodified standard MIT License text
Copyright line reads exactly: Copyright (c) 2026 Yazan
commands.model_reason: Verbatim boilerplate text with two fixed substitution values -- purely mechanical.

commands.title: Write CHANGELOG.md with 0.1.0 entry
commands.description: Write CHANGELOG.md for jot, following the Keep a Changelog style, containing a single entry for '0.1.0 -- initial release'. The entry should briefly note the initial feature set: add, list, search, and delete commands. Do not invent any other version entries or unreleased sections.
acceptance_criteria: CHANGELOG.md exists at the workspace root
Contains exactly one version entry, labeled 0.1.0, described as the initial release
Entry mentions the add/list/search/delete commands as the initial feature set
commands.model_reason: Single fixed changelog entry with a given feature list -- mechanical, no design judgment.

commands.title: Design note storage format and write STORAGE.md
commands.description: Decide and document, in STORAGE.md, how jot (a Python 3, single-user, single-machine, local-file CLI with no network sync and no concurrent multi-process writers) should store notes on disk. The design must satisfy three constraints simultaneously: (1) full-text search stays fast as the collection grows to tens of thousands of notes, (2) an edit or write that is interrupted by the process being killed mid-write must never corrupt the on-disk data, and (3) the format should remain readable/inspectable by hand (e.g. with a text editor or basic shell tools) where practical. Evaluate at least two rejected alternatives (for example: SQLite with FTS5, an append-only JSONL log with periodic compaction, and one-file-per-note with a separate search index) and give concrete reasons for rejecting each, tied to the three constraints above and to the Python 3 / single-writer / local-only context. State a clear final recommendation with its own trade-offs acknowledged.
acceptance_criteria: STORAGE.md exists at the workspace root
States a single clear recommended storage design/format
Explicitly addresses all three constraints: full-text search performance at tens-of-thousands-of-notes scale, crash-safety on a mid-write kill, and hand-readability
Documents at least two rejected alternatives with concrete reasons tied to the Python 3, single-user, single-machine, no-concurrent-writers context
Trade-offs of the chosen design are acknowledged, not just its benefits
commands.model_reason: The one substantive design task in this project -- requires weighing genuine engineering trade-offs (search performance vs. crash-safety vs. hand-readability) rather than mechanical writing.
